summary: ICRAA § 1786.40; CCRAA § 1785.20.5 (alternative); UCL § 17200; Penal Code § 290.46(j) (I&B — preliminary NSOPW / registry)

counts.title: [INDEPENDENT PATH] ICRAA, Civ. Code §§ 1786.40 and 1786.50 — rebuilt around the statute: advise that an investigative report was obtained and supply the ICRA name and address; October 5 letter names agencies and says consumer reports influenced the decision but does not give the investigative-report advice; not a 'failed to identify the decisive component' theory; 1786.52 discovery date does not appear on the face of the pleading
[ALTERNATIVE] CCRAA, Civ. Code §§ 1785.20.5 and 1785.31 — if the reports were ordinary consumer credit reports; I&B any later-completed component used on October 5 was not in the September 26 packet
[INDEPENDENT PATH] UCL § 17200 — unlawful prong cites 1786.40, 1785.20.5, and 290.46(j)(2)(E); unfair gravity/utility; standing vs restitution distinguished; four-year 17208 clock

[PLEADED ON INFORMATION AND BELIEF] Penal Code § 290.46(j) — last count on page one; NSOPW remained Processing on every snapshot furnished to Plaintiff; furnished packet contains neither a completed hit nor a completed no-record; inference that Swift used preliminary sex-offender-registry information from that in-process component, in whole or in part, in the Oct. 5 denial
[OMITTED] Tameny / IIED — two-year CCP § 335.1 clock from Sept. 26 / Oct. 5, 2023 closed in 2025
[OMITTED] FCRA — two-year 15 U.S.C. § 1681p discovery clock from the 2023 letters would have closed
[PRESERVED, NOT PLEADED] FEHA and Fair Chance Act — no CRD right-to-sue in the record; 2023 CRD window is closing
